name: Dull Lavender
lede: Dull Lavender is a pale, greyed pinkish lilac, the sort of color that sits on the edge between a purple and a neutral.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
The name goes back to Ridgway's color atlas of 1912, where a plate shows it, and it was carried into the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 [1]. It belongs to the neutrals in our library, a lilac with most of its chroma taken out [1]. Its nearest named neighbor is [[thistle]], about 7 units away, and it is also close to [[old-lavender]] and [[mountbatten-pink]] [1].

St Clair describes the paint of ships on the Cape Town run, whose hulls were an indeterminate dull lavender-gray-pink, set against scarlet funnels and white decks [2]. The same passage then turns to Lord Mountbatten aboard HMS Kelly [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive a color near this swatch appears in 55 of 23,781 paintings, or 0.23 per cent, and it most often plays the lightest tone in a painting [3]. [[painter:john-singer-sargent|Sargent]] has it in 5 of his 287 works here, 4.5 times the baseline of the museums those works come from [3]. It is most over-represented in the United States, at 3.6 times [3]. These are photographs of aged paintings, so read them as screen colors [3].
